title: Former Vice President of Software Engineering at Intel Believes Marvell’s Lumentum Deal Strengthens Its Growth Prospects Despite Execution and Supply Risks
expert: Former VP of Software Engineering at Intel (left mid-2025; Gaudi programs)
verdict: A former Intel VP (no direct Marvell view) expects no DSP share loss to Broadcom before 2028 and repeats a $30 billion custom-XPU trajectory, but sees HBM4 and CoWoS limits in 2027 delaying XPU revenue conversion.

Custom program roster and scope: $30 billion custom XPU within the next five years (hearsay), in line with the Investor Day custom \$30B FY31 (SB #64484). → Tenet 1 (custom) ↑
Interconnect growth rate: no DSP switch to Broadcom before 2028 (estimate); qualification takes years. → Tenet 2 (1.6T duopoly) →
Margins: laser fabs cut GM by a few points from around 57% (estimate), pressuring the low end of the 56–59% FY31 GM model (SB #64519). → Tenet 4 (GM dilution) ↓

changes: Custom XPU $30 billion within five years (hearsay) vs Investor Day custom $30B FY31 (SB #64484): consistent (echo of management).
GM down a few points from around 57% with fab ownership (estimate) vs FY31 GM model 56–59% (SB #64519) and Semtech call 2026-11-05 margin-dilution warning: consistent (lower).
Indium-phosphide laser supply "more manageable" later next year (estimate) vs 2026-11-05 Lightmatter and Semtech calls, Lumentum booked through early-to-late 2029: conflicting.
DSP customers unlikely to move to Broadcom before 2028 (estimate) vs Lightmatter call 2026-11-05 expecting customers to diversify to Broadcom/Credo: conflicting on timing.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (custom $10B+ FY29): ↑ — $30 billion custom-XPU trajectory; second-sourcing a generation needs about 1,000 people, so wins are sticky.
Tenet 2 (1.6T duopoly): → — no DSP switch to Broadcom before 2028, but 1.6T→3.2T is a competitive window in the next six to nine months.
Tenet 4 (opex leverage > GM dilution): ↓ — laser fabs could take GM a few points below around 57%.
Tenet 5 (bear flank): ↑ — Broadcom holds 60%–70% of custom compute; MediaTek and Alchip add competition.
